relations.evidence: You must have the [Organization Owner](../organization-user-roles.md#organization-role-organization-owner) role to manage realms.

relations.subject: auth:group-mapping
relations.evidence: If group mapping is on, Capella assigns roles to SSO users based on which teams map to which SSO groups.

relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (revokesRole) - deleting the realm's identity-provider link cascades into revoking every permission it granted, a management-plane analog of the data-plane REVOKE statement family
relations.evidence: When you delete a realm, Capella deletes the permissions of all SSO users connected to your organization through that realm.

relations.subject: auth:group-mapping
relations.evidence: If they sign in after you turn on group mapping, their roles sync based on any mapped SSO groups, and Capella deletes the old permissions.

relations.subject: auth:sso
relations.evidence: Every SSO user is a member of a realm's default team unless otherwise specified through [role mapping](manage-role-mapping.md).

relations.subject: auth:realm
relations.evidence: Realms manage the link with your identity provider (IdP). Each organization supports one realm. If you need to create a realm, see [Add SSO Authentication](add-sso-auth.md).

relations.subject: auth:group-mapping
relations.evidence: For more information about managing SSO users with group mapping turned off, see [Manage Organization Users](../manage-organization-users.md) and [Manage Project Users](../../projects/manage-project-users.md).

notable_absence.finding: This page (reached only after a realm already exists) never repeats the paid-support-plan gate seen on add-sso-auth.md/capella-ui-auth.md - it assumes SSO is already enabled and only re-states the Organization Owner role requirement. No edition badges or server-version-string citations either.

cross_component_finding: revokesRole (originally minted for the data-plane REVOKE SQL++ statement) turns out to generalize cleanly to this management-plane realm/group-mapping context - both realm deletion and a group-mapping-on resync are described with the same verb the docs use for permission removal ('Capella deletes the permissions'/'Capella deletes the old permissions'). This is a second confirmed reuse of a data-plane-originated predicate (after autoRegistersUser, reused from Sync Gateway) in the auth: family, suggesting the base relation vocabulary (grantsRole/revokesRole/autoRegistersUser) is genuinely product-agnostic even though the concepts it connects (auth:permission-set vs rbac-role:role vs sgw:role) are not.
